source_text: Qui est imago Dei invisibilis primogenitus omnis creaturae. Qui exit de hoc mundo ferens imaginem terreni ad nihilum redigitur in civitate Dei; caelestis imaginis insignia reportet.
orientation: Origen is closing the homily on Psalm 38 by contrasting the earthly image, which perishes, with the heavenly image of Christ, the firstborn of all creation.
pass_a_gloss: Who is [the] image of God [the] invisible firstborn of all creation. Who goes out of this world bearing [the] image of [the] earthly to nothing [he] is reduced in [the] city of God; of [the] heavenly image [the] marks [he] may carry back.

choices.why: The glossary for imago Dei speaks of bearing the marks of the heavenly image, so insignia is rendered as marks to match that language.
Reportet is a jussive subjunctive expressing a wish or exhortation; carry back preserves the prefix re- and the force of the command.
The passive of redigo with ad nihilum means to be brought to nothing or annihilated; reduced to nothing keeps the passive and the destination.
Terreni is a genitive singular masculine, referring to the earthly man or image; of the earthly one makes the personal reference explicit.

bible_refs.note: imago Dei invisibilis primogenitus omnis creaturae

pass_b_english: He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation (Colossians 1:15). Whoever goes out of this world bearing the image of the earthly one is reduced to nothing in the city of God; let him carry back the marks of the heavenly image.

last_rejected.quote: He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation (Colossians 1:15).
last_rejected.source_quote: Qui est imago Dei invisibilis primogenitus omnis creaturae.
last_rejected.why: Source uses 'Qui est' (relative clause), continuing description; English 'He is' makes it a new independent statement, changing syntax and possibly speaker attribution.
last_rejected.fix: who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation
last_rejected.ruling: Latin 'Qui est' opens Col 1:15 quote; 'He is' is standard biblical rendering, not a major change.

last_rejected.quote: is reduced to nothing in the city of God
last_rejected.source_quote: ad nihilum redigitur in civitate Dei
last_rejected.why: Latin 'ad nihilum redigitur' means 'is reduced to nothing,' but 'in civitate Dei' is where he should carry back marks, not where he is reduced to nothing; misjoined clauses.
last_rejected.fix: is reduced to nothing; in the city of God let him carry back the marks of the heavenly image
last_rejected.ruling: Latin syntax: 'ad nihilum redigitur in civitate Dei' attaches to same clause; semicolon separates 'reportet'. Translation is defensible.

last_rejected.why: English imperative 'let him' softens the Latin jussive/subjunctive 'reportet' (let him carry back/bring back) which is hortatory command, not permission.
last_rejected.fix: let him bring back the marks of the heavenly image
last_rejected.ruling: 'Let him carry' is standard jussive rendering; hortatory nuance preserved, not softened to mere permission.
